subject: gargoyle
pitch:
Category: Monster.
Subject: cathedral gargoyle crouched on a ledge.
Style: gothic stone carving.
reasoning:
I'm planning a moderate-sized module for a crouched gargoyle on a stone ledge, using flat stone colors with moss on top, and sketching out the joint skeleton starting from the root.

Designing the skeleton chain...

Checking the arm segment lengths against the shoulder-to-wrist distance confirms it works, so now I'm figuring out elbow bend direction for the crouched pose and setting up side-based naming conventions (s=1 as left/+X) before defining the arm chain's parent joint and naming scheme.

Now I'm sketching the hind leg geometry: haunch, knee, and foot positions for a crouched stance, checking segment lengths against the hip-to-foot distance so the knee bend direction looks right, with toe spikes added at the tip.

For the wings, I'm planning the arm chain from shoulder through elbow to wrist, folded up and outward with increasing height, then adding three finger chains radiating from the wrist to form the tips, with membranes stretched between them.

Still placing wing geometry...

For the torso I'm planning to sweep a chain of spine points from hips to neck using an elliptical radius profile that tapers at the ends and bulges at the chest.

Setting up the neck sweep with a narrower constant radius, then defining a head joint positioned at the end of the neck chain so it anchors correctly.

Building head parts now: a blocky skull using boxes with slight forward tilt, a muzzle extending forward as a smaller box, and a jointed jaw hinged below for articulation.

I'm adding teeth and fangs as small spikes projecting from muzzle and jaw, then positioning glowing amber eye spheres carefully on the skull's front surface with recessed dark sockets behind them.

Now I'm shaping brow ridges as tilted boxes, working out the rotation signs so angry brows slope inward-down and outward-up, mirroring the tilt direction based on side.

Next I'm moving to small nostril boxes on the muzzle tip, then setting up curved horns using a bezier sweep from a base point near the head, through a control point, to a tip, angling them back and upward.

Working out a local-point helper for head-relative offsets, then sketching bat-style pointed ears as extruded triangular slabs facing forward.

Actually I'll drop the ears and instead go with horns plus a spiky crest along the neck and back for that gargoyle look. For eyes I'm adding glowing spheres using a flat-colored standard material, plus a chin spike and maybe a lolling red tongue box for extra character. Now I'm thinking about rib details running along the spine.

Writing dorsal spike placement...

Scattering moss across upward-facing hits on torso and wings using flattened green sphere geometry, then adding claws at the hand/wrist tips using a ring arrangement for toes.

I'm reconsidering the claw placement since the ring approach ties toe direction to the path tangent, which points downward rather than forward. Instead I'll place toes manually as spikes pointing forward and down from a palm block at each hand position, which is simpler and more predictable than relying on ring tilt logic.

For bones, unspecified parts snap to the nearest joint, so I need to assign bones explicitly—props and static ledge pieces can ride the root joint via hips, while the ledge itself spans a defined height range as the base structure.

Now I'm sizing the ledge: a main slab roughly 1.5 wide by 1.9 deep to accommodate the gargoyle's tail-to-wingtip span, with a narrower lower slab and wider upper lip forming a cornice, plus thin seam boxes on the front face suggesting cut blocks, and some relief detailing with moss and drip stains for texture.

I'm also setting up a color palette for the stone, moss, eyes, horns, claws, tongue, and wings, planning cooler shadow tones beneath each form for depth.

For sectoring, I'm defining angle ranges per body part to apply light, base, and dark tones -- lighter on top, base in between, darker belly shading -- so the torso gets a believable countershaded look. I'm also planning muscle definition with small flat-shaded icosahedron blobs at the shoulders and haunches, and sketching out helper functions for generating icosahedrons and boxes.

Now I'm working through the limb geometry: tapered sweeps along the leg chains with varying radii for thighs and shins, blocky feet with spike-like toes, and rump blobs at the hips for added volume. For the wings, I'm sweeping tapered tubes along the arm and finger chains, then building membrane geometry that stretches between adjacent fingers starting from a shared wrist point, using the wing color for the skin.

Still working out finger tips and body edge points, then setting up the wing arm chain from shoulder through elbow and wrist into a catmull spline for the tip.

Neck needs to start where spine ends, using a round cap sweep, with the head attaching at the neck's endpoint. I'm settling on role names for each chain—spine, neck, tail, arm, leg, wing, digit, jaw, head—and working out the sweep radii along the torso from hips to chest to the neck base.

For the tail, I want a tapering sweep with pointed caps, then a spade-shaped tip extruded as a diamond outline at the very end.

Working out the orientation vectors for the tail tip piece, figuring out which axis should point along the tail's curving direction versus thickness.

Adjusting tail positions and radii...

Now mapping out the hip and spine joints for a crouched forward-leaning pose, then placing the neck and head points so the skull centers roughly a half-meter forward with the muzzle extending further out.

I'm computing the head position so it overhangs the ledge slightly for a gargoyle-like perch, adjusting the ledge's depth and z-center to accommodate that overhang, then setting up a helper function to convert local head-relative coordinates into world space.

Since the head is tilted downward a few degrees, I realize the box parts need to be oriented using the head's quaternion rather than plain world axes, so I'm working out how to pass the head's rotation into the box helper so each piece aligns naturally with the tilted skull.

For posing, I'm planning to pose the jaw joint slightly open after everything else is built, tipping it down a small number of degrees around the joint at the back of the mouth.

I'm now laying out the head's geometry with a helper that builds boxes from local offsets, starting with the skull block extending forward from the neck joint, then moving on to the cranium top piece.

For the brow ridge I'm working out how to tilt angled boxes by adjusting the up-vector rather than using rotation directly, since the helper only supports direction and an up parameter for rolling the box around its axis.

Resolved the tilt direction: up vector tilts toward −x for the brow angle, confirming the counterclockwise rotation logic. Now adding the muzzle box, nose bump, and nostril placements...

Still placing head parts...

Adding lower fangs, chin geometry, and incisor rows along the jaw...

Still shaping skull features...

Moving to torso: planning dorsal spikes, chest quatrefoil, shoulder blobs and spine plates, skipping detailed ribs for simplicity.

Now I'm working out shoulder and haunch icosahedron blobs at the joint positions, plus palm boxes for the hands. I'm figuring out the arm chain positions (shoulder, elbow, wrist) so the limbs emerge naturally from the chest, checking that the shoulder radius fits inside the chest sweep, and estimating where the arms reach forward so the hands land plausibly on a ledge.

I'm tweaking the target point and segment lengths so the arm bends slightly at the elbow rather than staying ramrod straight, then setting up the limb function with root, target, lengths, and bend direction, feeding the resulting points into a chain call with named joints and tapering sweep radii for the arm.

Now I'm working out wrist height to properly nest into the ledge, adding a palm box and clawed spikes, then moving to the hind legs — computing root-to-target distances and bend amounts so the knee juts forward, with a foot box and toe spikes capping the limb.

For the ledge itself, I'm planning scattered flat moss patches using squashed spheres placed with jitter, then thinking through seam lines and the front lip geometry of the ledge.

Still placing seam details...

I'm adding gothic surface touches too—drip stains as dark thin boxes under the lip, moss accents in cracks, and a small quatrefoil relief carved into the base's front face using a ring of cylinders plus a center one.

Writing quatrefoil placement...

Setting up spike placement along dorsal, neck, and tail sweeps using along() helpers to distribute them automatically with varying sizes.

For the wings, I'm defining bone hierarchies and sweep thicknesses for the arm, fingers, and wrist claw, plus a membrane connecting the chain edges for the bat-like skin, considering how edges read from current pose.

For embellishments, I'm adding a small glowing amber gem at the center of the chest quatrefoil alongside the eye glow, then setting up a moss helper that scatters small sphere geometry patches onto upward-facing torso surface hits to simulate moss growth.

Now I'm defining helper functions for building box-based parts attached to the head bone, handling positioning and orientation options, and preparing to construct the jaw parts with similar logic.

I'm reconsidering whether to compute local coordinate offsets manually using cross products instead of relying on uncertain helper assumptions — deriving forward, up, and left vectors explicitly so the positioning math is unambiguous and verified.

Setting up the jaw joint using the hp-based positioning, defining its parent, location, aim point, and role.

For the horn, I'm sweeping a bezier curve through base/control/tip points with tapering radius and flat-to-point caps, keeping ridges and collar details minimal for now. Overall part count looks reasonable at roughly 150-200, so I'm moving forward to actually write the full construction code.

Now I'm defining helper functions for icosahedron and box geometries, then working through the shoulder-to-hand limb construction for both left and right sides using the limb-building helper with shoulder/target points and bend directions.

Building the arm chains with named joints, sweeping stone geometry along them with tapering radii, adding an elbow spike for a knobby joint, and placing a box-shaped palm plus three small claw spikes at the fingertip positions...

Now I'm moving to the hind leg: setting up hip-knee-ankle joints with a limb chain, sweeping thicker thigh radii with a haunch bump, adding a foot box and toe spikes, plus a backward hock spike at the ankle.

Next I'm adding the haunch, shoulder, and rump as flattened ico shapes bound to their respective joints, then building a tail tip using an arrow extrude with bevel and horn coloring.

For positioning, I'm placing the arrow at the tail path's end point, bound to the last tail joint, with coloring sectors defined on the torso sweep to differentiate light and dark stone regions. Now I'm setting up the ledge details and double-checking the gargoyle's stance so the hind feet sit correctly, before moving into the torso spine chain setup.

I'm sweeping the neck using a tapered radius chain, adding mane spikes along it, then scattering mossy spheres across the ledge with randomized positions and sizes to add texture, before finalizing and returning the root node.

For scattering debris on the torso, I'm using hit-based placement to stick small embedded geometry with slight scale variation. Now I'm building a quatrefoil helper that generates petal shapes around a center point by computing a local basis from the surface normal, so the petals orient correctly against any facing direction.

Positioning the ledge-front cylinders so they protrude slightly from the surface, then adding a small glowing gem icosphere at the chest point using the glow import from the kits path. Now double-checking the head axis parameter before finalizing.

For the horn, I'm defining a curved bezier sweep from base to tip that curls backward, giving it a flat start cap and pointed end cap colored as horn material, skipping the extra ring detail. Then I'll write out the final result.
